1	# m5 data contracts (what test authors may rely on; implementers keep this file current)
     2	
     3	## Run identity and agent chat names
     4	- `args.blind` is a boolean, default false. `args.raid`, when supplied, is a non-empty single-line string and takes precedence over automatic selection. `launch.js stage --stage m5` also accepts `--raid <name>` and `--blind`.
     5	- `m5/raids.json` is `{theme, public, blind}`: a theme string and two ordered arrays of base names. The heist theme uses separate public and blind lists. Automatic selection skips names already present in `m5/raids_used.jsonl`; after the base names it cycles through the same list with suffixes `2`, `3`, etc. Explicit names are recorded too.
     6	- Each ledger row and `C/raid.json` has exactly `{raid, blind, run_root, utc}`; `run_root` is absolute and `utc` is an ISO UTC timestamp. Reservations are serialised. A run reuses its existing reservation and rejects conflicting raid/blind arguments. The launcher reserves against the original pipeline ledger before freezing its copy.
     7	- m5 sets `args.chat_prefix = "x-<raid>"`. Other scripts opt in using `args.chat_prefix`, an agent option `chat_prefix`, or the workflow flag `--chat-prefix`. Without a prefix, runner naming stays unchanged.
     8	- Names are `<chat_prefix>-<label>[-<descriptor>]`; labels are lowercased, non-`[a-z0-9-]` runs become `-`, edge hyphens are removed, and an empty label becomes `agent`. Concurrent sibling calls sharing a label within a stage add `1of<n>`, `2of<n>`, etc. Repair turns add `retry<k>` (starting at 1); fallback calls add `fb`. When needed together, descriptors appear in that order, separated by hyphens. Harness repair calls supply agent option `retry: 1`.
     9	- wf passes the name to every runner as `name`. OpenCode uses `--title`, Claude uses `--name`, and Codex prepends `[<name>]` as the first prompt line, before role instructions.
    10	
    11	## m5 model policy (workflow configuration)
    12	- m5 runs use `node idea/wf.js --config m5/wf_config.json --script m5/pipeline.js ... --profile latent_skeptic --family codex`, without `--disable-family claude`. `m5/wf_config.json` holds a `workflow` section identical to `idea/config.json`'s and an `understudy` section with: `primary_family: "codex"`, `mode: "fallback"`, `on_refusal: "halt"`, `disabled_families: []`, `chain: {"codex": ["opencode"], "opencode": ["codex"], "claude": ["codex"], "cursor": ["codex"]}`, and `routes: [{"match": "^skeptic-[45]$", "primary": "claude/sonnet"}, {"match": "^review$", "primary": "claude/sonnet"}, {"match": "^(intake|harness|[a-z]+-repair|seal|propose|tests|implement)$", "understudy": "claude/opus"}]`.
    13	- Effect: every authoring call (intake, harness, any `*-repair`, seal, propose, tests, implement) resolves to a Codex primary with `claude/opus` as its first understudy and OpenCode second (owner, 2026-10-30: Opus covers Codex authors when Codex fails). Skeptic ballots 1–3 resolve to a Codex primary with only OpenCode behind it; no Claude model appears in their primary or chain. Ballots 4–5 and the launch review resolve to `claude/sonnet` with Codex as the only understudy. A Claude refusal is not handed over (`on_refusal: "halt"`): the call returns null, so a refused ballot is a null ballot (it counts against the gate like a rejection) and a refused review fails as a missing review. Transport failures hand over to Codex as for any other call. Only `claude/sonnet` is routed (never Fable).
    14	- The pipeline writes `S/OPERATOR_TAKEAWAY.md` from validated signatures after all stage records, with the raid only in its header. `m5/operator_takeaway.py` accepts optional `--raid`; its Python `takeaway(records, raid=None)` API preserves the old header when omitted. Raid is not added to stage facts or v1 signature IDs.
    15	
    16	## A/intake/ (written by the intake agent; checked by the pipeline)
    17	- benchmark.json, data.json: non-empty JSON objects.
    18	- anchors.json: an array, possibly empty; each item has a unique non-empty string `id`, non-empty `quantity` and `source`, finite numeric `published_value`, and `tolerance`. Its length must equal facts.anchors_count. Zero is a valid published value or tolerance.
    19	  - An item is a reference when its comparison is `"=="` and its `tolerance` is null; every other item is an anchor. A reference records a published value without a published acceptance criterion: it is measured and reported, never passed or failed. Intake never invents a tolerance and never converts a published uncertainty into one.
    20	  - Optional `uncertainty` is null or exactly `{kind, value}`, where `kind` is `"standard_error"`, `"standard_deviation"` or `"interval_halfwidth"` and `value` is finite and nonnegative. It records published uncertainty where available and never affects scoring.
    21	  - Optional `comparison` is one of `"=="` (the default), `">"`, `">="`, `"<"`, or `"<="`. For `"=="`, an anchor passes when `abs(measured_value - published_value) <= resolved_absolute_tolerance`. For inequalities, it passes when `measured_value <comparison> published_value`; tolerance is ignored and may be 0 or null. Intake should specify `comparison` when the published criterion is a threshold.
    22	  - `tolerance` is a finite nonnegative number (absolute tolerance), or an object with exactly one key: `{"abs": x}` or `{"rel": x}`, where `x` is finite and nonnegative. For `"=="`, relative tolerance resolves to `x * abs(published_value)`; a zero reference therefore requires exact agreement.
    23	- baseline.json: non-empty repo, build_commands, run_commands and published_configuration, plus commit or pin. `build_commands` lists every command that builds or installs the baseline, including package-manager installs of released binaries, and is never empty. The intake prompt states both. The intake prompt names every key the completeness check reads exactly as the check reads it, as a JSON key: in baseline.json `repo`, `build_commands`, `run_commands`, `published_configuration`, and `commit` or `pin` (`pin` is any non-empty immutable identifier, such as a release, tag or content hash, when no commit exists); in EXECUTION.json `representative_scale`, `inputs`, `outputs` and `timing_scope`. It states that the check reads only these key names, so an equivalent value under another key does not count. The completeness check itself is unchanged.
    24	- EXECUTION.json: non-empty representative_scale, inputs, outputs and timing_scope. Optional `stage_budgets_s` supplies positive integer seconds in [1, 999999999], with keys `setup`, `anchors`, `profile`, `method_setup`, `method_run`, `tests`, `evaluate`. Keys `method_setup`, `method_run`, `tests` and `evaluate` each resolve independently from `EXECUTION.json.stage_budgets_s`, then `args.stage_budgets_s`, then defaults: method_setup=1200, method_run=1200, tests=900, evaluate=2400. Keys `setup`, `anchors` and `profile` resolve as the next bullet states (U47). Legacy `timeout_s` and `timeouts` no longer set pipeline box budgets. Every box command passes its resolved budget as `boxrun --timeout`. Harness uploads/probes use setup; implementation uploads, baseline snapshots, patch application and integrity checks use method_setup; evaluation uploads/integrity checks use method_setup. Script retries under the other keys retain the original budget.
    25	- Finish-first timing for the baseline workload (U47; owner direction 2026-10-30: intake's budgets are recorded estimates, not timeouts; a run is limited by a 12 h hard ceiling; a reproduction-only result counts). Keys `setup`, `anchors` and `profile` resolve from `args.stage_budgets_s` when the key is present there. Otherwise the budget is the time left before the run ceiling when that box command starts: `run_ceiling_s` minus the whole seconds elapsed since the pipeline script started, rounded down. `run_ceiling_s` is the optional `args.run_ceiling_s`, an integer in [1, 999999999], default 43200 (12 h); any other value is an invalid budget and is handled as an invalid stage budget is. Every box command under these keys resolves its budget when it starts: each setup and anchors attempt, each rerun after a repair, each identical retry, every harness upload, the box probe and its upload, the fixed profiler and the concurrency probe. When the time left is below 1 s, the command does not run and its step fails as a timeout does (`error_class: timeout`, exit 3). `EXECUTION.json.stage_budgets_s` values for these three keys stay in EXECUTION.json unchanged and never set a timeout. Prompts that state setup, anchors or profile budgets give the seconds resolved when the prompt is built and say the figure is the time left before the run ceiling, not a target; one fixed scale and no scale search still apply. The other keys are unchanged. Run evidence (blind-01 run8, 2026-10-31): intake set a 1,200 s anchors budget; in two of three anchors attempts the representative-scale workload was still running at the budget, it completed only partly and wrote no measurements, and an authorized reader judged an anchors budget from a measured or published runtime the smallest fix; the materials were not implicated. The profile stage runs the same `run_command.sh`.
    26	- Every harness, test-author, method-author and repair prompt states the budget for each script it writes. All require one fixed scale from EXECUTION.json, no scale search or doubling loops, and completion well within the budget. Baseline run_evaluation.sh and method run_anchors.sh use method_run per invocation; evaluate bounds each complete scorer, including all repetitions and curves.
    27	- The intake passes only when the files are complete and found is true, data is "available", licence is not "restricted", and stock_environment is not false. Missing executable inputs and an explicit licence restriction block; missing published tolerances do not. A `licence` of "unknown" does not block: local experiments proceed under the owner's standing authorization (2026-10-30), which is recorded separately from licence evidence and never changes it. Intake records `licence` and `licence_basis` as the evidence shows and never relabels ambiguous coverage as permission. The intake prompt states that "unknown" stays "unknown" when permission is not established, that it does not stop the run, and that "restricted" does. `found` means a public benchmark with executable published code, command and inputs; a benchmark without published tolerances qualifies, with its published values recorded as references. The intake prompt states this.
    28	- Intake facts add optional `anchored` (boolean): true exactly when anchors.json holds at least one anchor. Every executed intake stage emits it once anchors.json validates; it is null when anchors.json is missing or invalid and on SKIPPED/stub records. `OPERATOR_TAKEAWAY.md` shows it among the intake gate flags. A run whose intake has `anchored=false` is unanchored: its claims concern the workload as published and run, not agreement with published values.
    29	- An intake FAIL signature names the failed gate conditions in v1 `blockers`, from the existing blocker vocabulary and in this fixed order: `licence` when the `licence` fact is "restricted", `data_unavailable` when the `data` fact is "partial", "unavailable" or "unknown", and `env_irreproducible` when the `stock_environment` fact is false. Each condition is read from the facts the record carries, whatever else failed (missing reply, incomplete or invalid files, or `found` false); a null or absent fact adds no blocker. When no condition applies, and for every PASS, SKIPPED and stub intake, `blockers` stays `["none"]`. Intake `exit_code`, `exit_kind` and `error_class` are unchanged. `OPERATOR_TAKEAWAY.md` lists these blockers in its Blockers section as for any stage.
    30	- Intake facts add optional `licence_basis`, the basis of the licence judgement for the least-covered item among the benchmark code and its required inputs. It is the first of these values that applies to any item, in this fixed order: `"unreachable"` (the licence evidence for the item could not be fetched), `"none"` (no licence, terms of use or owner statement found for the item), `"owner"` (the item's only basis is a permission stated by the run's owner in the brief), `"distribution"` (the item's only basis is a licence of the repository, package or archive that distributes it, and that licence does not state that it covers the item), `"explicit"` (a licence or terms of use states that it covers the item, by name, by path, or as the whole repository, package or archive). The intake prompt defines these values and asks for the fact; a value outside the list makes the reply invalid, as for any other fact. It is null when the reply omits it, and on SKIPPED and stub records. It never changes the gate, the `licence` fact, `blockers` or any other fact. Signatures carry it as an enum fact, and `OPERATOR_TAKEAWAY.md` shows it among the intake gate flags.
    31	- `OPERATOR_TAKEAWAY.md` shows the intake `licence` fact among the intake gate flags, next to `licence_basis`. When intake PASSes with `licence` other than "permitted", the takeaway adds exactly one line: "Execution authority: owner's standing instruction (2026-10-30), not licence evidence." No other record carries the authorization, and no fact changes because of it.
    32	
    33	## A/results/probe/probe.json (collected before the harness agent)
    34	- The pipeline uploads the committed `m5/box_probe.sh` and runs it through boxrun in the same remote working directory as the harness. Both operations write receipts under `C/receipts/`, using the setup timeout. Fetched `out/probe.json` is validated as a JSON object and copied to `A/results/probe/probe.json`. Logs and fetched `out/` remain under `A/results/probe/`. Stale local or remote probes cannot satisfy a new run.
    35	- Fields match the probe script:
    36	  - `os`: null or `{id, version_id, pretty_name, version, name}` from `/etc/os-release`, with nullable strings; `kernel`: string or null.
    37	  - `nproc`, `memory_kb` (MemTotal in KiB), `disk_home_avail_bytes` (available bytes on `$HOME`'s filesystem): integers or null.
    38	  - `nvidia`: null or `{gpus, driver_version, cuda_version}`; `gpus` is an array of GPU name strings, versions are strings or null. CUDA here is the driver's reported CUDA version.
    39	  - `nvcc`: an array of `{path, version}` for deduplicated executable paths from `command -v nvcc`, `/usr/local/cuda*/bin/nvcc`, and `/usr/lib/cuda*/bin/nvcc`; `version` is captured `nvcc --version` text or null. Missing nvcc yields `[]`.
    40	  - `cmake`, `gcc`, `g++`, `make`, `git`, `python3`, `pip`: null or `{path, version}`, with a string path and nullable version text. `pip` falls back to `pip3`.
    41	  - `apt_sources`: an array of `{file, lines}` naming apt source files and their lines mentioning cuda or nvidia. Commented matches may be included when no uncommented matches exist; these do not authorize enabling a repository. Missing matches yield `[]`.
    42	  - `apt_enabled_sources`: an array of `{file, entries}` covering every apt source the image enables, whatever it mentions: for `/etc/apt/sources.list` and `/etc/apt/sources.list.d/*.list`, `entries` holds each line whose first token is `deb` (commented lines are excluded); for `/etc/apt/sources.list.d/*.sources` (deb822), `entries` holds one string per stanza not marked `Enabled: no`, joining its `Types`, `URIs`, `Suites` and `Components` fields as `Types: <v> URIs: <v> Suites: <v> Components: <v>` (absent fields omitted). Files with no entries are omitted; none yields `[]`. `apt_sources` is unchanged. Both fields read the apt directory `${M5_PROBE_APT_DIR:-/etc/apt}` (its `sources.list` and `sources.list.d/`), so tests can point the probe at a fixture; the pipeline never sets this variable.
    43	  - `sudo_nopasswd`: boolean indicating whether `sudo -n true` succeeds.
    44	- Individual missing tools or unavailable facts yield null/empty collections without failing the probe. Probe upload/run failure, nonzero boxrun exit, failed fetch, or missing/invalid JSON fails reproduce with `error_class: infra`, before any harness call; the probe has no agent repair; a timeout permits the single identical command retry defined below.
    45	- Full JSON content is included in the harness prompt and every setup and anchor repair prompt. Agents must use discovered paths and versions and never hard-code a toolkit path absent from the probe. Select a CUDA toolkit root discovered in `probe.json` with both `include/cuda_runtime.h` and `lib64/libcudart.so`, checking both with `ls` on the box from the scripts. Pass it explicitly via `CUDAToolkit_ROOT` or `-DCMAKE_CUDA_COMPILER=<root>/bin/nvcc`, and prepend `<root>/bin` to `PATH`. Never rely on `/usr/bin/nvcc` when a complete toolkit root exists. A tool or system library the published baseline needs but the stock image lacks may be installed with `sudo apt-get install -y` from any source the probe reports in `apt_enabled_sources` (after `sudo apt-get update`), once `apt-cache policy <package>` shows an install candidate. Never add repositories, keys or source lines, and never enable a commented or disabled source. Setup prints each package it installs and its installed version (`dpkg-query -W <package>`). Otherwise only cmake may fall back to pip. If neither route applies, scripts must fail with a clear message. The harness prompt and every setup and anchors repair prompt state this rule. Run evidence (blind-01 run6, 2026-10-31): setup failed three times on a missing runtime library packaged in the Ubuntu archive (universe); the rule then allowed apt only from the CUDA/NVIDIA lines in `apt_sources`, so neither repair could install it.
    46	
    47	## A/harness/ (written by the harness agent or copied from a previous run)
    48	- Optional `args.harness_from` is a non-empty directory path to a previous run's `A/harness/`, resolved relative to the pipeline working directory. After a successful fresh box probe, the pipeline copies the exact bytes of `setup.sh`, `run_anchors.sh` and `run_command.sh` into the current `A/harness/` and skips the initial harness agent call. If present, `run_evaluation.sh` is copied too. Missing or unreadable required scripts, or an invalid argument, fail reproduce with `error_class: parse`; there is no fallback harness generation. Without this argument, harness generation is unchanged.
    49	- Reuse writes script-owned `C/harness_source.json` as `{source, files}`. `source` is the absolute source harness directory; `files` maps each copied filename to `{sha256, modified}`. `sha256` is the lowercase 64-digit SHA-256 of the exact original copied bytes and remains unchanged after repair. `modified` starts false and becomes true after an accepted repair of that script, before its upload/rerun, even if that rerun fails. Reuse permits the same bounded setup and anchor repairs (at most four for setup, two for anchors) as generated harnesses; every repair receives the fresh probe. Reuse adds no stage facts and does not reuse probe results, measurements, or stock verification.
    50	- `setup.sh`, `run_anchors.sh`, `run_command.sh` are bash scripts. The pipeline invokes them as `bash harness/<name>` from one fresh `/tmp/m5-<uuid>` directory on the already-running operator-managed box. They share that directory across reproduce and profile. No dev lifecycle commands are issued. `BOX` and `FETCH` are inherited unchanged by `boxrun.sh`, including injected executables.
    51	- Harness uploads (the initial upload of every harness script, and the re-upload of rewritten scripts after each accepted repair) use the implement upload encoding, so no process argument or remote command line grows with script size. For each script, the upload truncates `harness/<name>` (`: > harness/<name>`) and then appends its base64 in independently decodable chunks of at most 24,576 characters (`printf %s <chunk> | base64 -d >> harness/<name>`); an empty script is created empty. These lines are batched in order into boxrun commands below 32,768 characters. Every batch begins with `set -e` and `mkdir -p harness out`, runs as operation `upload` under the setup budget, and has its own receipt. A batch that fails (nonzero exit, failed fetch, missing receipt, or a timeout after its identical retry) ends the upload: later batches are not sent and the harness script does not run, and the step fails as a failed upload does today (`infra`, or `timeout` on a timeout). After all batches succeed, the uploaded files are byte-identical to the local harness files. A harness small enough for one batch uploads in exactly one `upload` command, as before. Run evidence (blind-01 run5, 2026-10-31): the single upload command exceeded the operating system's 131,072-byte limit on one argument, spawning boxrun failed with E2BIG before any receipt was written, and reproduce stopped with `infra` before setup ran.
    52	- `setup.sh` installs/builds the exact published baseline in the stock image; sudo is allowed only for apt. Published source/configuration stays under `baseline-published/`; inputs stay under `data/`. Setup builds and checks only the baseline; the fixed pipeline profiler owns profiling tools and installation. Setup must tolerate one retry in the same directory. Tuning is deferred.
    53	- `run_anchors.sh` runs the published protocol at the intake's representative scale and writes `out/anchors_measured.json` as an object mapping each intake item ID (anchors and references) to a finite measured number; with an empty anchors.json it still runs the published command and writes `{}`. Missing or non-numeric measurements fail the corresponding anchor; booleans and nonfinite values count as non-numeric. Additional measurements are ignored for scoring.
    54	- `run_command.sh` contains only the exact measured baseline command and complete environment at the representative scale, including working directory, arguments, CUDA visibility and GPU count. It runs the published binary, saves its output for anchor parsing, and propagates its exit status. `run_anchors.sh` invokes `bash harness/run_command.sh` from the shared working directory without overriding its environment or duplicating the command. Profiling invokes that same file from that same directory. No agent writes profiling scripts or profile outputs.
    55	- `run_command.sh` uses paths relative to its working directory, never absolute paths into the run directory, and writes only under `out/` or temporary files. The concurrency probe and evaluation run it from sibling work directories that link the same trees (see Concurrency probe). Harness and repair prompts state this requirement.
    56	- Optional unit files (U50): `run_units.sh` and `units.json`, used only by the unit-mode concurrency probe. `units.json` is exactly `{"units": [...]}` with at least four entries, in the order the published full run processes them, each exactly `{id, outputs, cost_s}`: `id` is a unique string matching `^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._:+=-]{0,127}$` by which the published program selects that unit; `outputs` is a non-empty array of unique relative paths naming that unit's result files under `out/`, each one or more `/`-separated components made of `[A-Za-z0-9._+=-]`, none of them `.` or `..`; `cost_s` is a finite positive number, the unit's own seconds as recorded in the reproduce run's logs or outputs. `bash harness/run_units.sh <id>...` runs the exact measured command of `run_command.sh` (same binary, configuration, environment and scale) restricted to the listed units (one or more), using the published program's own subset selection, in the order given. It obeys every `run_command.sh` rule (relative paths, writes only under `out/` or temporary files, no `CUDA_MPS_*` changes), writes each listed unit's `outputs` under `out/` at the same paths as the full run, and propagates the exit status. Under `args.harness_from`, each of the two files present in the source is copied with its exact bytes and recorded in `C/harness_source.json` like the scripts. Files present in `A/harness/` are uploaded with the initial harness upload (same encoding and batching), never later. No repair changes them: after every setup or anchors repair the pipeline restores their bytes (or their absence), as it restores `run_evaluation.sh`. The harness agent is not asked to write them; fresh harness generation is unchanged. The probe's comparison with the frozen baseline outputs (see Concurrency probe) is their validation.
    57	- The pipeline owns CUDA MPS. No harness script (`setup.sh`, `run_anchors.sh`, `run_command.sh`, `run_evaluation.sh`) may set, unset or override any `CUDA_MPS_*` environment variable, or start or stop an MPS daemon; the scripts inherit these variables unchanged. Harness and repair prompts state this rule. (Method code written in implement is not a harness script and may manage MPS itself.)
    58	- Harness prompts require the published build and binary to run and measurements to come from their OUTPUT. Scripts must never parse or assert on source text. Measurement checks fail only on missing or invalid output; deterministic scoring owns anchor comparisons.
    59	- Without `args.harness_from`, there is one initial agent call (`harness`, `ls-writer`, `sonnet`). Setup permits up to four repairs (`harness-repair`) and anchors up to two (`anchors-repair`) after a nonzero exit, with the same role/model. Each repair receives the failure class and at most the last 200 log lines of the latest failed attempt, and its prompt states its attempt number and the step's limit (`repair attempt <n> of <limit>`). Each later repair runs only after the previous repaired script ran and failed again (nonzero exit or output-gate error); a declined (null) repair, an infrastructure or fetch failure, or a failed upload ends the step. Owner direction 2026-10-30: finish experiments rather than stop them on a fixable failure; a blind run spent its one setup repair on a build-dependency failure, the repair worked, and setup then failed on a different import error that a single repair could not reach. U46 run evidence (blind-01 run7, 2026-10-31): setup spent both of its two repairs on successive script errors; each repair's log tail held its error, each repair targeted it and none regressed, a static check before upload would have caught none, and setup reruns reuse the materials already fetched and verified, so an attempt after a repair costs tens of seconds; an authorized reader judged more repairs of the same kind the smallest sufficient fix. Anchors keep two repairs until a run shows otherwise. The setup repair may rewrite only `setup.sh`. The anchors step executes `run_anchors.sh` and the `run_command.sh` it invokes, so the anchors repair may rewrite either or both and nothing else; a rewritten `run_command.sh` still obeys every `run_command.sh` rule above, and the anchors repair prompt states this. After each repair every rewritten script is recopied, then the step reruns once, with its budget resolved at the rerun's start (U47). Under reuse, an accepted anchors repair marks `modified` true for each of the two scripts whose bytes it changed. Infrastructure/fetch failures do not trigger repairs. Timeouts use the same repairs (the step's own limit), never an extra one. Repair prompts include budget seconds, measured wall seconds and max(0, wall_s-budget_s) overrun seconds. Profiling has no agent repair or execution retry; output/gate failures stop downstream work.
    60	
    61	## A/results/reproduce/ and deterministic anchor scoring
    62	- Every reproduce box command fetches remote `out/` into `A/results/reproduce/out/`, and its `<receipt-id>.log` into `A/results/reproduce/`. Logs remain in the agent view. The local fetched `out/` is cleared before each command to prevent stale measurements. The final copy contains the anchor run's outputs. When reproduce passes, the pipeline freezes those outputs on the box: through boxrun, as operation `reproduce-freeze` under the `setup` budget, it runs `test ! -e reproduce-out` and then `cp -a out reproduce-out` in the shared run directory. Like every reproduce command, its fetch replaces `A/results/reproduce/out/`, so that local copy and remote `reproduce-out/` hold the same outputs: the baseline outputs the seal and the test author read. Later stages never write to `reproduce-out/`; remote `out/` after reproduce also collects profiler and probe outputs and further runs of the baseline command, which are not baseline outputs.    239	
   240	```json

   242	  "evaluation_inputs": {"ids": ["input-0", "input-1"], "pin": "immutable input specification"},
   243	  "sample_sizes": {"inputs": 2, "seeds": 1},
   244	  "equivalence_metrics": [{"name": "accuracy", "tolerance": {"abs": 0.001}, "source": "scientific requirement citation"}],
   245	  "paired_seed_tests": {"kind": "deterministic", "justification": "scientific reason"},
   246	  "confidence_rule": {
   247	    "equivalence": {"kind": "paired_median", "confidence": 0.95},
   248	    "performance": {"kind": "paired_median", "confidence": 0.95}
   249	  },
   250	  "timing_scope": {"kind": "process_wall", "gpu_synchronization": "adapter", "description": "includes launch, transfer, compute and merge"},
   251	  "hardware_cost_basis": {"baseline_gpus": 1, "method_gpus": 1, "budget_unit": "gpu_s"},
   252	  "warmup": 1,
   253	  "repetitions": 7,
   254	  "scheduling_order": {"kind": "randomized_pairs", "seed": 42},
   255	  "minimum_worthwhile_gain": 1.05,
   256	  "compute_budgets": [60, 120, 240],
   257	  "equal_outcome_target": {"metric": "accuracy", "comparison": ">=", "target": 0.9}
   258	}
   259	```
   260	
   261	- Input IDs are unique nonempty strings. Records must cover exactly the Cartesian product, in seed-major then input-ID order. `sample_sizes.inputs` and `.seeds` are integer counts that must match the fixed lists. Deterministic runs use one null seed. Stochastic protocols use `{kind:"paired_median", seeds:[unique integers]}` instead; the same seeds apply to both arms. Input pins/specifications and splits remain part of the complete sealed protocol supplied to each adapter.
   262	- Metrics have unique nonempty `name`, nonempty `source` and tolerance. Deterministic tolerance is a finite nonnegative absolute number, `{abs:x}` or `{rel:x}`. Each paired row must satisfy `abs(method-baseline) <= tolerance`; relative tolerance multiplies `abs(baseline)`, including exact agreement at zero. All reported metric values must be finite numbers, never booleans.
   263	- Stochastic metrics require absolute tolerance. For each metric and seed, average the paired method-minus-baseline differences over fixed inputs. Use an exact sign-test confidence interval for the median of those seed averages. Equivalence requires the entire interval inside `[-tolerance,+tolerance]`, including endpoints. Bonferroni divides the two-sided error probability across sealed metrics. This tests equivalence of the median paired effect defined by the seal; it is not a failure-to-reject difference test.
   264	- Confidence is finite in `[0.5,1)`. For sorted samples `x` of length `n`, select the largest `k >= 1` with `P(Binomial(n,0.5) < k) <= alpha/2` for equivalence or `<= alpha` for performance. Equivalence bounds are `[x[k-1],x[n-k]]`; performance uses lower bound `x[k-1]` and an unbounded upper endpoint represented by null. No admissible `k` means insufficient measurements and VOID. At 95%, one metric needs at least six independent seed pairs; performance needs at least five timing pairs. More metrics or greater confidence can require more seeds. No bootstrap randomness or asymptotic approximation is used.
   265	- `warmup` is an integer >=0, measured but excluded from performance statistics; `repetitions` is an integer >=5. Each pair contains one run of each arm in independently shuffled order from Python's `random.Random(sealed_seed)`. Warmup pairs and curve arm order use the same RNG stream. Both arms use the same box, sealed inputs, seeds, configuration and scope. Published baseline is never tuned.
   266	- `timing_scope.kind` is `process_wall` (trusted `perf_counter` around the complete adapter subprocess) or `reported_wall` (adapter's measured `wall_s`, for scopes requiring program timers). Both arms must echo the exact sealed scope. Adapters must synchronize all used GPUs before completion/timer stop and include launch/transfer/merge overhead required by the scope. Missing or mismatched scope is VOID. Reported timings are actual program measurements, never extrapolated estimates.
   267	- `hardware_cost_basis` declares positive integer GPU counts per arm, bounded by both box and probe capacity. `C/box.json.price_usd_h` must be finite and positive. Per-GPU tariff is box hourly price divided by available box GPUs; run USD is measured seconds times GPUs used times this tariff /3600. Pair speedup is baseline seconds / method seconds; `speedup_published` is the median pair speedup. `cost_ratio` is the median paired method-USD / baseline-USD ratio. `equal_cost` means `cost_ratio <= 1`. Performance requires matched scientific outputs on warmups and timed pairs, the sealed one-sided confidence lower bound >= `minimum_worthwhile_gain`, and equal cost. `prediction_ratio` divides median speedup by the selected sealed interval's midpoint. Zero or unavailable pricing cannot establish equal cost.
   268	- Curves use GPU-second budgets. Each invocation receives the sealed budget and is bounded by both its script timeout and budget / GPUs used.     18	  - `anchors` preserves intake order and contains `{id, kind, published_value, measured_value, tolerance, passed}` for every item, with `kind` `"anchor"` or `"reference"`.     29	  - `c4-2`, `c2-2`, `b-2`, `a-2`: the same arms again in reverse order, to balance drift.
    30	  Each invocation's stdout and stderr go to `out/concurrency/logs/<work directory name>.log` of the shared run directory, and its environment is inherited unchanged. An arm's wall runs on a monotonic clock from launching its first invocation to the exit of its last.

    49	- Receipts use the boxrun format: `{name, rc, timed_out, wall_s, budget_s, overrun, fetched, started_utc, ended_utc, gpu_busy_s, gpu_busy_known}`. `name` is the receipt ID; `rc` is an integer remote exit code or null; `timed_out` and `fetched` are booleans; `wall_s` is nonnegative integer elapsed seconds; `budget_s` is the positive integer timeout supplied to boxrun; `overrun` is boolean, true on timeout or when measured wall_s exceeds budget_s; timestamps are UTC strings.     50	- Failed reproduce/profile signatures have fixed `error_class`: `infra` for unavailable box execution/receipts, failed upload, or failed fetch after a successful command, or a fixed profiler infrastructure marker; `install` for failed setup after the bounded repairs; `anchor` for an anchor-run failure or a failed anchor; `parse` for missing/invalid output files, unavailable harness files, or a nonzero profile command exit; `numeric` for a parsed profile that fails the stage-count, process-wrapper, coverage, or GPU telemetry gate. Exit codes are 4 for anchor failures, 3 for timeouts and 2 for the other failures. `infra` is added to the shared v1 error-class enum so the v2 envelope remains v1-valid. Box/fetch stdout and stderr are never copied into operator signatures.
    51	- Any box receipt with rc=124 or timed_out=true records a timeout, even when fetch fails. A final timeout fails its stage with `error_class: timeout`, exit 3. Authored setup and anchor scripts consume their existing repairs (at most four for setup, two for anchors), and method/test scripts their one bounded repair; method/test timeout repairs expose only the fixed timeout count plus budget/elapsed/overrun seconds, never test content. Transport, patch, probe, integrity and immutable evaluator commands permit one identical retry under the same budget (under keys `setup`, `anchors` and `profile`, the budget resolved at the retry's start, U47), without editing scientific payloads or trusted scorers. A second timeout stops that operation and stage. The fixed profiler permits no repair or execution retry; its first timeout stops profiling with `error_class: timeout`.
    52	- Reproduce, profile, implement and evaluate facts optionally add exactly typed timeout fields `{timed_out: boolean, budget_s: nonnegative integer, overrun: boolean}` when a box timeout occurs. `timed_out=true` records any attempt timing out, `budget_s` is the latest timed-out command's budget, and `overrun` is true when any timed-out receipt overruns. These fields survive a successful bounded repair; stage status then reflects the repaired result. Older records and SKIPPED/stub records retain their existing fact keys. No command output or new free-text fields enter signatures.
    53	- Numeric ratio facts accept finite JSON numbers, including integer spellings such as `0` and `1`; booleans remain invalid. This permits fully timed profiles to emit the capped fraction `1`.
    54	- Every stage records its own elapsed wall-clock seconds in v1 `wall_s`, excluding signature emission. SKIPPED stages measure only their skip handling, never the prior stage's duration.
    55	- Runner results add boolean `tokens_known`, true when the provider reports input/output usage (including reported zeros). wf exposes `agent.usage()` as a cumulative snapshot `{calls, tokens_in, tokens_out, unknown}`; `unknown` counts runner attempts without usage.     56	- Stages aggregate reported input/output counts into v1 `tokens_in`/`tokens_out`; `facts.tokens_known` is true only when every runner attempt in that stage reports usage. Unknown counts retain numeric zero placeholders required by v1. `gpu_busy_known` reflects box receipt telemetry for reproduce/profile (see Compute metadata); harness profile evidence is reported separately. Downstream scientific stages are skipped after either failed gate; takeaways still runs.
    57	
    58	## A/bounds.json (computed before the seal agent)
    59	- `python3 m5/bounds.py <profile-packet.json> <out.json>` writes an atomic JSON object keyed by the five menu methods. Exit 0 means success; exit 1 means invalid/missing input or unavailable output, with content-free diagnostics. Legacy packets without `gpu_count` default to 1. GPU counts must be nonnegative integers.
    60	- Explicit stage `kind` takes precedence. Without it, lowercase stage names are split into ASCII alphanumeric tokens. Any token `transfer`, `transfers`, `h2d`, `d2h`, `htod`, `dtoh`, `copy`, `memcpy`, `upload`, or `download` means transfer; otherwise any token `compute`, `kernel`, `kernels`, `inference`, `training`, `forward`, or `backward` means compute. All other names mean other. Other stages and unmeasured time remain serial.
    61	- The fixed mapping and maximum factors are:
    62	
    63	  | Method | Acts on | p | Maximum factor k | bound |
    64	  | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
    65	  | data-parallel over inputs | whole workload | 1 | min(8, factor) | k |

     1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
     2	# run_units.sh - the measured baseline restricted to original prepared manifest rows.
     3	#
     4	# Invoked as:  bash harness/run_units.sh <system_id:kind>...   (working directory = the shared run directory, or a sibling
     5	# work directory that links baseline-published/, data/ and harness/). Command paths are relative.
     6	# Runtime absolute PATH entries and TMPDIR are inherited from run_command.sh; see REPORT.md.
     7	# PATH entries are resolved from this working directory because the published
     8	# FroDock adapter changes directory into a temporary stage directory.
     9	#
    10	# Representative scale (EXECUTION.json, fixed): the 8 preregistered PINDER-S apo-paired systems in
    11	# data/selection.json, requested holo/apo jobs only, n_solutions=50, mpi_np=8, force=false,
    12	# docked by the published `pinder_methods predict --method frodock` and scored by the published
    13	# `pinder_eval` (50 decoys per selected job). FroDock is CPU + MPI only: no GPU is used (CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES="",
    14	# GPU count 0). CUDA MPS variables are inherited unchanged.
    15	#
    16	# Output (stdout+stderr of both published commands): out/run_command/run_command.log
    17	#   decoys:  out/results/frodock/<pinder_id>/{holo,apo}_decoys/model_<rank>.pdb
    18	#   scores:  out/results/frodock_metrics.csv, out/results/frodock_leaderboard.csv
    19	# Exit status: nonzero if either published command fails.
    20	set -Eeuo pipefail
    21	[ "$#" -gt 0 ] || { echo "ERROR: at least one system_id:kind is required" >&2; exit 2; }
    22	
    23	# ------------------------------------------------------------------ complete environment
    24	export CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=""          # CPU/MPI-only baseline
    25	BASELINE_GPU_COUNT=0
    26	N_SOLUTIONS=50
    27	MPI_NP=8
    28	FORCE=false
    29	EVAL_MAX_WORKERS=8
    30	METHOD=frodock
    31	export PINDER_BASE_DIR=data
    32	export PINDER_RELEASE=2024-02
    33	export LOG_LEVEL=INFO
    34	export PYTHONUNBUFFERED=1
    35	unset PINDER_DATA_DIR || true
    36	# CUDA toolchain selection (same ls-checked rule as setup.sh; not used by the CPU baseline)
    37	CUDA_SEL=""
    38	for root in /usr/local/cuda /usr/lib/cuda; do
    39	  if ls "$root/bin/nvcc" "$root/include/cuda_runtime.h" "$root/lib64/libcudart.so" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    40	    CUDA_SEL="toolkit_root:$root"; export PATH="$root/bin:$PATH"; export CUDAToolkit_ROOT="$root"; break
    41	  fi
    42	done
    43	if [ -z "$CUDA_SEL" ] && ls /usr/bin/nvcc /usr/include/cuda_runtime.h /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libcudart.so >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    44	  CUDA_SEL="distro:/usr/bin/nvcc"
    45	fi
    46	[ -n "$CUDA_SEL" ] || { echo "ERROR: no complete CUDA layout found (same rule as setup.sh)" >&2; exit 1; }
    47	VENV=baseline-published/venv
    48	VPY="$VENV/bin/python"
    49	export PATH="$PWD/baseline-published/frodock/bin:$PWD/$VENV/bin:$PATH"
    50	export PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1
    51	
    52	# ------------------------------------------------------------------ output locations (logs preserved)
    53	RUN_DIR="out/run_command"
    54	RESULTS="out/results"
    55	mkdir -p "$RUN_DIR/history"
    56	TS="$(date -u +%Y%m%dT%H%M%S%NZ)"
    57	if [ -e "$RUN_DIR/run_command.log" ]; then
    58	  mkdir -p "$RUN_DIR/history/$TS"
    59	  mv "$RUN_DIR"/*.log "$RUN_DIR"/*.yaml "$RUN_DIR"/*.json "$RUN_DIR"/*.tar.gz "$RUN_DIR/history/$TS/" 2>/dev/null || true
    60	fi
    61	# Preserve decoys and scoring output from earlier invocations as well as logs.
    62	if [ -d "$RESULTS" ]; then
    63	  mkdir -p "$RUN_DIR/history/$TS"
    64	  mv "$RESULTS" "$RUN_DIR/history/$TS/results"
    65	fi
    66	exec > >(tee "$RUN_DIR/run_command.log") 2>&1
    67	mkdir -p out/tmp
    68	export TMPDIR="$PWD/out/tmp"
    69	
    70	for f in "$VPY" "$VENV/bin/pinder_methods" "$VENV/bin/pinder_eval" data/selection.json data/frodock/frodock_setup.csv; do
    71	  [ -e "$f" ] || { echo "ERROR: $f missing; run harness/setup.sh first" >&2; exit 1; }
    72	done
    73	for b in frodockgrid_mpi_gcc frodock_mpi_gcc frodockcluster_gcc frodockview_gcc soap.bin; do
    74	  [ -e "baseline-published/frodock/bin/$b" ] || { echo "ERROR: FroDock $b missing" >&2; exit 1; }
    75	done
    76	
    77	# fresh results tree: force=false would otherwise skip jobs whose decoys already exist
    78	mkdir -p "$RESULTS"
    79	cat > "$RUN_DIR/frodock_config.yaml" <<EOF
    80	n_solutions: $N_SOLUTIONS
    81	mpi_np: $MPI_NP
    82	force: $FORCE
    83	EOF
    84	# The published predict loop reads this CSV directly; select original rows below.
    85	# No preprocessing, regenerated inputs, extra prediction entry point, or output tree.
    86	
    87	# ------------------------------------------------------------------ printed configuration (validated)
    88	"$VPY" - "$RUN_DIR/frodock_config.yaml" "$RESULTS/frodock_setup.csv" data/selection.json \
    89	    "$METHOD" "$N_SOLUTIONS" "$MPI_NP" "$FORCE" "$EVAL_MAX_WORKERS" "$BASELINE_GPU_COUNT" "$@" <<'PY'
    90	import json, os, re, sys, yaml
    91	import pandas as pd
    92	from pinder.core import get_index
    93	cfg = yaml.safe_load(open(sys.argv[1])); jobs = pd.read_csv("data/frodock/frodock_setup.csv"); sel = json.load(open(sys.argv[3]))
    94	idx = get_index()
    95	s = idx[idx["pinder_s"].astype(bool)]
    96	apo = s[s["apo_R"].astype(bool) & s["apo_L"].astype(bool)]
    97	ids = sorted(set(apo["id"]))[: sel["n"]]
    98	print(f"PINDER_S_SYSTEM_COUNT={s['id'].nunique()}")
    99	print(f"PINDER_S_APO_PAIRED_COUNT={apo['id'].nunique()}")
   100	print("SELECTED_IDS=" + json.dumps(ids))
   101	errs = []
   102	if sys.argv[4:10] != ["frodock", "50", "8", "false", "8", "0"]: errs.append("actual command parameters differ from fixed configuration")
   103	if os.environ.get("CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES") != "": errs.append("CPU baseline must expose zero GPUs")
   104	if os.environ.get("PINDER_BASE_DIR") != "data" or os.environ.get("PINDER_RELEASE") != "2024-02": errs.append("dataset environment differs from fixed configuration")
   105	if ids != sel["ids"]: errs.append("selection from index differs from data/selection.json")
   106	if sel["n"] != 8 or len(ids) != 8: errs.append("representative scale must contain exactly 8 systems")
   107	if cfg != {"n_solutions": 50, "mpi_np": 8, "force": False}: errs.append(f"config {cfg} is not the published representative config")
   108	if sorted(set(jobs["id"])) != sorted(ids): errs.append("frodock_setup.csv ids differ from selection")
   109	if sorted(set(jobs["kind"])) != ["apo", "holo"] or len(jobs) != 2 * len(ids): errs.append("frodock_setup.csv is not holo+apo for every id")
   110	if set(zip(jobs["id"], jobs["kind"])) != {(pid, kind) for pid in ids for kind in ("holo", "apo")}: errs.append("frodock_setup.csv lacks an expected id/pairing")
   111	# Select only complete, original records in the requested order. The published
   112	# entry point consumes this setup CSV (preserved source patch, lines 17-20).
   113	requested = sys.argv[10:]
   114	keys = [pid + ":" + kind for pid, kind in zip(jobs["id"], jobs["kind"])]
   115	if len(set(keys)) != len(keys): errs.append("duplicate prepared unit")
   116	if len(set(requested)) != len(requested): errs.append("duplicate requested unit")
   117	if any(not re.fullmatch(r"[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._:+=-]{0,127}", key) or key not in keys for key in requested):
   118	    errs.append("unknown or invalid unit id")
   119	if errs:
   120	    sys.exit("ERROR: " + "; ".join(errs))
   121	jobs = jobs.iloc[[keys.index(key) for key in requested]]
   122	jobs.to_csv(sys.argv[2], index=False)
   123	print(f"CONFIG method=frodock subset=pinder-s pairs=holo,apo n_jobs={len(jobs)} n_solutions={cfg.get('n_solutions')} "
   124	      f"mpi_np={cfg.get('mpi_np')} force={cfg.get('force')} CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES='{os.environ.get('CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES')}' "
   125	      f"host_nproc={os.cpu_count()} PINDER_BASE_DIR={os.environ.get('PINDER_BASE_DIR')}")
   126	if errs:
   127	    sys.exit("ERROR: " + "; ".join(errs))
   128	PY
   129	echo "GPU_COUNT=$BASELINE_GPU_COUNT CUDA_SELECTION=$CUDA_SEL MPIRUN=$(command -v mpirun) FRODOCK_BIN=$(dirname "$(command -v frodock_mpi_gcc)")"
   130	echo "PINDER_VERSION=$("$VPY" -c 'import importlib.metadata as m;print(m.version("pinder"))')"
   131	
   132	# ------------------------------------------------------------------ published docking command
   133	set +e
   134	"$VPY" "$VENV/bin/pinder_methods" predict --method "$METHOD" --data_dir data/frodock \
   135	    --results_dir "$RESULTS" --subset pinder-s --pairs all --config "$RUN_DIR/frodock_config.yaml"
   136	PRED_RC=$?
   137	set -e
   138	echo "PREDICT_EXIT=$PRED_RC"
   139	[ "$PRED_RC" -eq 0 ] || { echo "ERROR: pinder_methods predict exited $PRED_RC" >&2; exit "$PRED_RC"; }
   140	
   141	# FroDock 3.12 writes small molecules as HETATM with a blank chain. The published adapter
   142	# concatenates receptor + transformed ligand without restoring that label. Restore only blank
   143	# ligand HETATM labels, retaining every atom, coordinate, rank and all other PDB bytes. Identify the
   144	# ligand suffix by its existing L-labelled atoms. FroDock's output atom count need not equal the
   145	# input reader's count (e.g. alternate locations); validate emitted records, not that equality.
   146	# Keep original decoys and a change manifest beside the saved command output.
   147	"$VPY" - "$RESULTS" "$RUN_DIR" <<'PY'
   148	import csv, json, sys, tarfile
   149	from pathlib import Path
   150	import biotite.structure.io as strucio
   151	
   152	results, run_dir = map(Path, sys.argv[1:])
   153	changes = []
   154	with tarfile.open(run_dir / "raw_decoys.tar.gz", "w:gz") as originals:
   155	    for job in csv.DictReader(open(results / "frodock_setup.csv")):
   156	        directory = results / "frodock" / job["id"] / (job["kind"] + "_decoys")
   157	        for model in sorted(directory.glob("model_*.pdb")):
   158	            lines = model.read_text().splitlines(keepends=True)
   159	            atom_lines = [i for i, line in enumerate(lines) if line.startswith(("ATOM  ", "HETATM"))]
   160	            if not atom_lines or lines[atom_lines[0]][21:22] != "R":
   161	                raise SystemExit(f"ERROR: {model}: missing receptor prefix")
   162	            restored = []
   163	            in_ligand = False
   164	            for line_index in atom_lines:
   165	                line = lines[line_index]
   166	                chain = line[21:22]
   167	                if chain == "L":
   168	                    in_ligand = True
   169	                    continue
   170	                if chain == "R" and not in_ligand:
   171	                    continue
   172	                if not in_ligand or chain != " " or not line.startswith("HETATM"):
   173	                    raise SystemExit(f"ERROR: {model}: unexpected chain on PDB line {line_index + 1}")
   174	                restored.append(line_index + 1)
   175	            if not in_ligand:
   176	                raise SystemExit(f"ERROR: {model}: missing labelled ligand atoms")
   177	            if restored:
   178	                originals.add(model, arcname=model.relative_to(results))
   179	                for line_number in restored:
   180	                    line = lines[line_number - 1]
   181	                    lines[line_number - 1] = line[:21] + "L" + line[22:]
   182	                model.write_text("".join(lines))
   183	                changes.append({"file": str(model), "line_numbers": restored, "chain": "L"})
   184	            chains = set(strucio.load_structure(str(model)).chain_id)
   185	            if chains != {"R", "L"}:
   186	                raise SystemExit(f"ERROR: {model}: invalid chains {chains}")
   187	json.dump(changes, open(run_dir / "chain_labels_restored.json", "w"), indent=2)
   188	print(f"CHAIN_LABELS_RESTORED models={len(changes)} atoms={sum(len(c['line_numbers']) for c in changes)}")
   189	PY
   190	
   191	# ------------------------------------------------------------------ published scoring command
   192	# pinder_eval asks for interactive confirmation for every subset/pairing with systems not run here;
   193	# answer yes so the published missing-system penalty is applied (no --allow_missing).
   194	set +e +o pipefail
   195	yes y | "$VPY" "$VENV/bin/pinder_eval" --eval_dir "$RESULTS" --method_name "$METHOD" --max_workers "$EVAL_MAX_WORKERS"
   196	EVAL_RC=${PIPESTATUS[1]}
   197	set -e -o pipefail
   198	echo "EVAL_EXIT=$EVAL_RC"
   199	[ "$EVAL_RC" -eq 0 ] || { echo "ERROR: pinder_eval exited $EVAL_RC" >&2; exit "$EVAL_RC"; }
   200	exit 0

run10_harness2/run_command.sh
     1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
     2	# run_command.sh - the exact measured baseline command and its complete environment.
     3	#
     4	# Invoked as:  bash harness/run_command.sh   (working directory = the shared run directory, or a sibling
     5	# work directory that links baseline-published/, data/ and harness/). All paths are relative to that
     6	# working directory. PATH entries are resolved from this working directory because the published
     7	# FroDock adapter changes directory into a temporary stage directory.
     8	#
     9	# Representative scale (EXECUTION.json, fixed): the 8 preregistered PINDER-S apo-paired systems in
    10	# data/selection.json, holo and apo pairings (16 docking jobs), n_solutions=50, mpi_np=8, force=false,
    11	# docked by the published `pinder_methods predict --method frodock` and scored by the published
    12	# `pinder_eval` (800 decoys). FroDock is CPU + MPI only: no GPU is used (CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES="",
    13	# GPU count 0). CUDA MPS variables are inherited unchanged.
    14	#
    15	# Output (stdout+stderr of both published commands): out/run_command/run_command.log
    16	#   decoys:  out/results/frodock/<pinder_id>/{holo,apo}_decoys/model_<rank>.pdb
    17	#   scores:  out/results/frodock_metrics.csv, out/results/frodock_leaderboard.csv
    18	# Exit status: nonzero if either published command fails.
    19	set -Eeuo pipefail
    20	
    21	# ------------------------------------------------------------------ complete environment
    22	export CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=""          # CPU/MPI-only baseline
    23	BASELINE_GPU_COUNT=0
    24	N_SOLUTIONS=50
    25	MPI_NP=8
    26	FORCE=false
    27	EVAL_MAX_WORKERS=8
    28	METHOD=frodock
    29	export PINDER_BASE_DIR=data
    30	export PINDER_RELEASE=2024-02
    31	export LOG_LEVEL=INFO
    32	export PYTHONUNBUFFERED=1
    33	unset PINDER_DATA_DIR || true
    34	# CUDA toolchain selection (same ls-checked rule as setup.sh; not used by the CPU baseline)
    35	CUDA_SEL=""
    36	for root in /usr/local/cuda /usr/lib/cuda; do
    37	  if ls "$root/bin/nvcc" "$root/include/cuda_runtime.h" "$root/lib64/libcudart.so" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    38	    CUDA_SEL="toolkit_root:$root"; export PATH="$root/bin:$PATH"; export CUDAToolkit_ROOT="$root"; break
    39	  fi
    40	done
    41	if [ -z "$CUDA_SEL" ] && ls /usr/bin/nvcc /usr/include/cuda_runtime.h /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libcudart.so >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    42	  CUDA_SEL="distro:/usr/bin/nvcc"
    43	fi
    44	[ -n "$CUDA_SEL" ] || { echo "ERROR: no complete CUDA layout found (same rule as setup.sh)" >&2; exit 1; }
    45	VENV=baseline-published/venv
    46	VPY="$VENV/bin/python"
    47	export PATH="$PWD/baseline-published/frodock/bin:$PWD/$VENV/bin:$PATH"
    48	export PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1
    49	
    50	# ------------------------------------------------------------------ output locations (logs preserved)
    51	RUN_DIR="out/run_command"
    52	RESULTS="out/results"
    53	mkdir -p "$RUN_DIR/history"
    54	TS="$(date -u +%Y%m%dT%H%M%S%NZ)"
    55	if [ -e "$RUN_DIR/run_command.log" ]; then
    56	  mkdir -p "$RUN_DIR/history/$TS"
    57	  mv "$RUN_DIR"/*.log "$RUN_DIR"/*.yaml "$RUN_DIR"/*.json "$RUN_DIR"/*.tar.gz "$RUN_DIR/history/$TS/" 2>/dev/null || true
    58	fi
    59	# Preserve decoys and scoring output from earlier invocations as well as logs.
    60	if [ -d "$RESULTS" ]; then
    61	  mkdir -p "$RUN_DIR/history/$TS"
    62	  mv "$RESULTS" "$RUN_DIR/history/$TS/results"
    63	fi
    64	exec > >(tee "$RUN_DIR/run_command.log") 2>&1
    65	mkdir -p out/tmp
    66	export TMPDIR="$PWD/out/tmp"
    67	
    68	for f in "$VPY" "$VENV/bin/pinder_methods" "$VENV/bin/pinder_eval" data/selection.json data/frodock/frodock_setup.csv; do
    69	  [ -e "$f" ] || { echo "ERROR: $f missing; run harness/setup.sh first" >&2; exit 1; }
    70	done
    71	for b in frodockgrid_mpi_gcc frodock_mpi_gcc frodockcluster_gcc frodockview_gcc soap.bin; do
    72	  [ -e "baseline-published/frodock/bin/$b" ] || { echo "ERROR: FroDock $b missing" >&2; exit 1; }
    73	done
    74	
    75	# fresh results tree: force=false would otherwise skip jobs whose decoys already exist
    76	mkdir -p "$RESULTS"
    77	cat > "$RUN_DIR/frodock_config.yaml" <<EOF
    78	n_solutions: $N_SOLUTIONS
    79	mpi_np: $MPI_NP
    80	force: $FORCE
    81	EOF
    82	cp data/frodock/frodock_setup.csv "$RESULTS/frodock_setup.csv"   # predict reads <results_dir>/frodock_setup.csv
    83	
    84	# ------------------------------------------------------------------ printed configuration (validated)
    85	"$VPY" - "$RUN_DIR/frodock_config.yaml" "$RESULTS/frodock_setup.csv" data/selection.json \
    86	    "$METHOD" "$N_SOLUTIONS" "$MPI_NP" "$FORCE" "$EVAL_MAX_WORKERS" "$BASELINE_GPU_COUNT" <<'PY'
    87	import json, os, sys, yaml

    27	# Building docker images for physics-based docking methods
    28	
    29	For convenience, we provide [dockerfiles](../../../../docker/) for building images with pinder and its dependencies pre-installed, along with the docking software. We do not provide the source software.
    30	
    31	In order to build the images, you will need to obtain the source software from the respective methods we support:
    32	* [FRODOCK](https://chaconlab.org/modeling/frodock/frodock-donwload)
    33	* [HDOCKlite](http://huanglab.phys.hust.edu.cn/software/hdocklite/)
    34	* [PatchDock](http://bioinfo3d.cs.tau.ac.il/PatchDock/download.html)
    35	
    36	Once downloaded, you need to provide a local path to the software compressed in `.tar.gz` format. See [expected software archive contents](#expected-software-archive-contents) for a detailed tree of the expected contents of the archive.
    37	
    38	When you are ready to build, you can run:
    39	```
    40	docker build --build-arg FRODOCK_SOURCE_ARCHIVE=./frodock.tar.gz -t pinder-frodock -f docker/frodock/Dockerfile.frodock .
    41	docker build --build-arg HDOCK_SOURCE_ARCHIVE=./hdock.tar.gz -t pinder-hdock -f docker/hdock/Dockerfile.hdock .
    42	docker build --build-arg PATCHDOCK_SOURCE_ARCHIVE=./patchdock.tar.gz -t pinder-patchdock -f docker/patchdock/Dockerfile.patchdock .
